messages.author: fe049c2835236bb1
messages.subject: Re: Projections work
parts:
Huy is right, you will just need to make sure that your rasters are in the same projection. And also be aware that the buffer units are in the same units as your coordinate reference system, which means that if you input UTM data you will need to enter 10000 for a 10 km buffer.

We’re working right now on better functionality for testing raster projections that are input by users, and we’ll keep you updated on any progress.

Jamie

messages.author: d73691b565754184
messages.subject: Re: Projections work
parts:
Hello,

Unfortunately, there is not possible to use a projected coordinate system on Wallace (e.g. NAD 83 California Teale Albers). I suggest you to transform your data to WGS84 (the geographic coordinates system that Wallace use). You can use the spTranform function to re-project your points () and projectRaster() for your raster.

Best,
Gonzalo
